nagpur.name: Deekshabhoomi
nagpur.description: World's largest hollow Buddhist stupa where Dr. B. R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism with over 600,000 followers on Ashok Vijaya Dashami in 1956.
nagpur.address: South Ambazari Road, Vasant Nagar, Dhantoli, Nagpur, Maharashtra 440020
nagpur.audio_guide_text: Welcome to Deekshabhoomi, the sacred monument where Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar led the historic Buddhist revival movement on October 14, 1956. The great stupa rises 120 feet into the air, constructed from Dholpur sandstone.

nagpur.name: Sitabuldi Fort
nagpur.description: Historic fortress built by the Bhonsle dynasty, site of the historic 1817 Battle of Sitabuldi fought between Mudhoji II Bhonsle and the British East India Company.
nagpur.audio_guide_text: Perched atop twin hillocks in central Nagpur, Sitabuldi Fort witnessed the pivotal battle of 1817. The fort houses memorials to fallen soldiers and offers panoramic views across the orange city.
nagpur.verified_source: Archaeological Survey of India / Indian Army Verified 2026

nagpur.name: Futala Lake & Promenade
nagpur.description: Scenic 200-year-old reservoir built by the Bhonsle Kings, famous for evening sunset views, illuminated fountains, and bustling street food stalls.
nagpur.address: Futala Lake Road, Telangkhedi, Nagpur, Maharashtra 440001
nagpur.audio_guide_text: Futala Lake was created by the Bhosle rulers of Nagpur over two centuries ago. Spanning 60 acres, it is Nagpur's favorite gathering spot for serene lakeside strolls and local street snacks.

nagpur.name: Ambazari Lake & Botanical Garden
nagpur.description: Nagpur's largest freshwater lake and origin of the Nag River, fringed by lush botanical mango groves, walking trails, and musical fountains.
nagpur.address: Ambazari Road, Ram Nagar, Nagpur, Maharashtra 440033
nagpur.audio_guide_text: Ambazari takes its name from 'Amba' (mango in Marathi) due to the historic royal mango orchards that surrounded it. Spanning over 15 square kilometers, it is a haven for migratory waterfowl.

nagpur.name: Raman Science Centre & Planetarium
nagpur.description: Affiliated with National Council of Science Museums, named after Nobel Laureate Sir C.V. Raman, featuring interactive physics galleries, a modern planetarium, and prehistoric park.
nagpur.address: Subhash Road, Gandhi Sagar, Empress City, Nagpur, Maharashtra 440018
nagpur.audio_guide_text: Named in honor of Nobel Laureate Sir C.V. Raman, this science center features interactive physics demonstrations, optical illusion halls, a 133-seat planetarium, and animated dinosaur models.

nagpur.name: Nagpur Central Museum (Ajab Bangla)
nagpur.description: Established in 1863, one of the oldest museums in India, holding rare antiquities from the Indus Valley Civilization, Mughal weapons, Gond sculptures, and dinosaur fossils.
nagpur.address: Civil Lines, Near GPO, Nagpur, Maharashtra 440001
nagpur.audio_guide_text: Known locally as Ajab Bangla, this museum was founded in 1863 by Sir Richard Temple. Its galleries house priceless 2,000-year-old stone sculptures, Maratha armaments, and fossilized dinosaur remains.

nagpur.name: Shree Ganesh Mandir Tekdi
nagpur.description: Ancient 250-year-old Swayambhu Ganpati shrine situated on a hillock (Tekdi) near Nagpur Railway Station, revered as the patron protector of Nagpur.
nagpur.audio_guide_text: Tekdi Ganesh Mandir is one of Nagpur's most venerated religious landmarks. The deity is a self-manifested (Swayambhu) rock idol that dates back to the era of the Bhonsle kings.

nagpur.name: Zero Mile Stone & Heritage Park
nagpur.description: Historic marker erected by the Great Trigonometrical Survey of British India in 1907, representing the geographical center of undivided India.
nagpur.address: Wardha Road, Civil Lines, Nagpur, Maharashtra 440001
nagpur.audio_guide_text: The Zero Mile Stone was erected in 1907 during the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India. It consists of an obelisk pillar and four stucco horses, used as the benchmark to measure all road distances across the subcontinent.
nagpur.verified_source: Survey of India / NMC Heritage Cell 2026

mumbai.name: Gateway of India
mumbai.description: Majestic 26-meter basalt triumphal arch built in 1924 overlooking the Arabian Sea, blending Indo-Saracenic and Muslim architectural styles.
mumbai.audio_guide_text: The Gateway of India was built to commemorate the 1911 visit of King George V. In February 1948, the last British battalion, the Somerset Light Infantry, marched through this arch, marking the end of colonial rule.

mumbai.name: Marine Drive (Queen's Necklace)
mumbai.description: World-famous 3.6-kilometer C-shaped coastal promenade along Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road, famed for Art Deco architecture and sunset sea breeze.
mumbai.address: Marine Drive, Churchgate to Nariman Point, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400020
mumbai.audio_guide_text: Marine Drive is lined with the world's second-largest collection of Art Deco buildings after Miami Beach, earning it UNESCO World Heritage status. At night, its streetlights resemble a glittering necklace of pearls.

mumbai.name: Elephanta Caves (Gharapuri)
mumbai.description: UNESCO World Heritage rock-cut cave temples dating from 5th to 7th centuries on Elephanta Island, featuring the masterpiece 20-foot Trimurti Shiva sculpture.
mumbai.best_time_to_visit: 09:00 AM (Take early ferry from Gateway of India)
mumbai.audio_guide_text: Carved directly into basalt cliff faces, Cave 1 contains the celebrated Trimurti sculpture depicting Shiva in three forms: Creator, Preserver, and Destroyer.

mumbai.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT)
mumbai.description: UNESCO World Heritage Victorian Gothic revival architectural landmark designed by F.W. Stevens, serving over 3 million commuters daily.
mumbai.audio_guide_text: Completed in 1887 to celebrate Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee, CSMT blends Victorian Italianate High Gothic with traditional Indian palace domes and stone-carved animals.

mumbai.name: Haji Ali Dargah
mumbai.description: 15th-century mosque and tomb of Sufi saint Pir Haji Ali Shah Bukhari, perched on an islet 500 meters offshore connected by a tidal causeway.
mumbai.best_time_to_visit: 09:00 AM (Low tide hours for easy causeway walk)
mumbai.address: Dargah Rd, Haji Ali, Worli, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400026
mumbai.audio_guide_text: Haji Ali Dargah sits 500 meters into the Arabian Sea. The narrow stone pathway is submerged during high tide, leaving the white marble sanctuary appearing to float on open waters.

delhi.name: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
delhi.description: UNESCO World Heritage fortress constructed by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1639, crafted from red sandstone along the Yamuna River.
delhi.address: Netaji Subhash Marg, Lal Qila, Chandni Chowk, New Delhi 110006
delhi.audio_guide_text: The Red Fort served as the ceremonial and political center of the Mughal Empire for nearly 200 years. Within its massive octagonal walls lie the Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, and Moti Masjid.

delhi.name: Qutub Minar & Iron Pillar
delhi.description: UNESCO World Heritage 72.5-meter fluted red sandstone minaret built in 1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, alongside the rust-resistant 1,600-year-old Gupta Iron Pillar.
delhi.audio_guide_text: Qutub Minar is the world's tallest brick minaret, featuring five distinct storeys with balcony overhangs and Quranic inscriptions. In the courtyard stands the famous 4th-century iron pillar.

delhi.name: Humayun's Tomb
delhi.description: UNESCO World Heritage garden tomb commissioned by Empress Bega Begum in 1565; the architectural prototype that inspired the Taj Mahal.
delhi.address: Mathura Road, Nizamuddin East, New Delhi 110013
delhi.audio_guide_text: Designed by Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, Humayun's Tomb was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, introducing the charbagh quadrilateral layout.

delhi.name: India Gate & National War Memorial
delhi.description: 42-meter triumphal arch memorial honoring 84,000 soldiers, fronted by Kartavya Path and the Amar Jawan Jyoti eternal flame.
delhi.address: Kartavya Path, India Gate, New Delhi 110001
delhi.audio_guide_text: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and completed in 1931, India Gate commemorates Indian troops who died during the First World War. The names of over 13,000 soldiers are inscribed onto its surfaces.

agra.name: Taj Mahal
agra.description: UNESCO World Heritage ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna River, commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan in 1631 for Mumtaz Mahal.
agra.address: Dharmapuri, Forest Colony, Tajganj, Agra, Uttar Pradesh 282001
agra.audio_guide_text: Considered the pinnacle of Mughal architecture, the Taj Mahal took over 20 years to construct. Its luminous Makrana marble features exquisite pietra dura inlay work using semi-precious lapis lazuli and jade.

agra.name: Agra Fort (Lal Qila Agra)
agra.description: UNESCO World Heritage 94-acre red sandstone fortress, the main imperial residence of Mughal emperors from Akbar to Aurangzeb.
agra.address: Agra Fort, Rakabganj, Agra, Uttar Pradesh 282003
agra.audio_guide_text: Agra Fort contains palatial quarters including the Jahangiri Mahal, Khas Mahal, and the Musamman Burj where Shah Jahan was imprisoned by his son Aurangzeb with a view of the Taj Mahal.

agra.name: Fatehpur Sikri
agra.description: Magnificent fortified Mughal ghost city built by Emperor Akbar in 1571, featuring the monumental Buland Darwaza and Jama Masjid.
agra.address: Fatehpur Sikri, Agra District, Uttar Pradesh 283110, India
agra.audio_guide_text: Step into Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar short-lived imperial capital. The Buland Darwaza, or Gate of Magnificence, towers 54 meters above the courtyard.

agra.name: Mehtab Bagh (Moonlight Garden)
agra.description: Charbagh garden complex located across the Yamuna River, perfectly aligned with the Taj Mahal for sunset viewing and photography.
agra.address: Dharmapuri, Forest Colony, Nagla Devjit, Agra, Uttar Pradesh 282001, India
agra.audio_guide_text: Mehtab Bagh, the Moonlight Garden, was built by Emperor Babur and later integrated by Shah Jahan as the ultimate vantage point for viewing the Taj Mahal reflected in the Yamuna.

paris.name: Eiffel Tower (Tour Eiffel)
paris.description: Wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars, designed by Gustave Eiffel for the 1889 World's Fair; globally recognized symbol of Paris and France.
paris.address: Champ de Mars, 5 Av. Anatole France, 75007 Paris, France
paris.audio_guide_text: Standing 330 meters tall, the Eiffel Tower was the world's tallest man-made structure for 41 years. Built from 18,000 puddle iron components and 2.5 million rivets, it sparkles with 20,000 bulbs every hour after sunset.
paris.verified_source: Societe d'Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel (SETE) 2026

paris.name: Louvre Museum (Musée du Louvre)
paris.description: World's largest and most visited art museum, housed in the historic Louvre Palace, holding 380,000 objects including the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Winged Victory.
paris.audio_guide_text: The Louvre began as a 12th-century medieval fortress under King Philip II. Today, its galleries extend over 72,000 square meters beneath I.M. Pei's celebrated glass pyramid entrance.

jaipur.name: Amber Fort (Amer Palace)
jaipur.description: Majestic 16th-century hilltop fortress famed for its artistic Hindu-Rajput elements, Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace), and Maota Lake panoramic views.
jaipur.audio_guide_text: Welcome to Amber Fort. Constructed by Raja Man Singh in 1592, this fort blends Rajput red sandstone with Mughal marble architecture. As you enter through Suraj Pol (Sun Gate), notice the Diwan-e-Aam and the world-famous Sheesh Mahal, inlaid with convex Belgian glass mirrors that illuminate the entire hall with a single candle flame.
jaipur.verified_source: Archaeological Survey of India / Tavily Verified 2026

jaipur.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
jaipur.description: Iconic pink sandstone facade featuring 953 honeycomb jharokhas (casements) designed for royal ladies to observe street life without being seen.
jaipur.address: Hawa Mahal Rd, Badi Choupad, J.D.A. Market, Jaipur 302002
jaipur.audio_guide_text: Standing before Hawa Mahal, you are gazing upon an architectural crown shaped like the deity Lord Krishna. Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, its honeycomb structure harnesses the Venturi wind effect to maintain cool natural air conditioning even during sweltering desert summers.

jaipur.name: City Palace Jaipur
jaipur.description: Grand royal residence housing the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum, opulent courtyards, Peacock Gate, and giant sterling silver vessels.
jaipur.address: Tulsi Marg, Gangori Bazaar, J.D.A. Market, Jaipur 302002
jaipur.audio_guide_text: City Palace remains the ceremonial seat of the Jaipur royal family. The Pritam Niwas Chowk features four renowned doorway gates representing the four seasons, including the mesmerizing Peacock Gate symbolizing autumn.

jaipur.name: Jantar Mantar Observatory
jaipur.description: UNESCO World Heritage site featuring 19 architectural astronomical instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial measuring time to 2 seconds precision.
jaipur.address: Gangori Bazaar, J.D.A. Market, Pink City, Jaipur 302002
jaipur.audio_guide_text: Commissioned in 1734 by astronomer-king Sawai Jai Singh II, Jantar Mantar is a masterwork of stone geometry. The towering Samrat Yantra sundial stands 27 meters tall and projects shadows accurately tracking celestial movements.

jaipur.name: Jal Mahal (Water Palace Promenade)
jaipur.description: Picturesque palace submerged in Man Sagar Lake against the Aravalli hills, offering scenic lakeside strolls and street photography.
jaipur.address: Amer Rd, Jal Mahal, Amber, Jaipur 302002
jaipur.audio_guide_text: Jal Mahal appears to float on the waters of Man Sagar Lake. While the interior is preserved for bird conservation, its promenade is Jaipur's favorite twilight stroll, illuminated by golden floodlights as migratory birds settle across the lake.

jaipur.name: Albert Hall Museum (Central Museum)
jaipur.description: Oldest museum in Rajasthan, set in an Indo-Saracenic masterpiece, housing ancient miniature paintings, Persian carpets, and an Egyptian mummy.
jaipur.best_time_to_visit: 14:00 PM (Ideal indoor sanctuary during afternoon heat or rain)
jaipur.address: Museum Rd, Ram Niwas Garden, Kailash Puri, Adarsh Nagar, Jaipur 302004
jaipur.audio_guide_text: Albert Hall opened in 1887, named after King Edward VII. The building is a triumph of Indo-Saracenic architecture. Inside, discover rare 16th-century Persian carpets, royal ivory carvings, and the famous Ptolemaic Egyptian mummy.
jaipur.verified_source: State Directorate of Archaeology / Tavily Verified 2026

jaipur.name: Panna Meena ka Kund (Hidden Stepwell)
jaipur.description: Intricate 16th-century symmetrical geometric stepwell and hidden architectural gem near Amber, renowned for hypnotic crisscross stairways.
jaipur.audio_guide_text: Panna Meena ka Kund is a historic rainwater harvesting stepwell. Notice the brilliant geometric stair pattern designed so that no person can descend and ascend using the exact same steps in sequence.

jaipur.name: Johari Bazaar & Heritage Street Food
jaipur.description: Vibrant historic bazaar famous for handmade Kundan jewellery, tie-dye bandhani textiles, and street-food icons like Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar (LMB).
jaipur.audio_guide_text: Johari Bazaar is the beating commercial heart of Jaipur's Pink City. Here, generations of silversmiths and gemstone cutters have traded since Sawai Jai Singh founded the grid city in 1727.

ujjain.name: Shree Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
ujjain.description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva and the only south-facing (Dakshinmukhi) Jyotirlinga in the world. Revered for its dawn Bhasma Aarti and the sprawling Mahakal Lok cultural corridor.
ujjain.audio_guide_text: Welcome to Shree Mahakaleshwar Temple, the cosmic center of time and eternity in ancient Hindu geography. As the only south-facing Jyotirlinga, Lord Mahakal is believed to conquer death itself. Walk through the newly restored Mahakal Lok corridor adorned with 108 sculpted pillars depicting Shiva cosmic lore.
ujjain.verified_source: Shri Mahakaleshwar Temple Management Committee (SMTMC) & MP Tourism 2026

ujjain.name: Kal Bhairav Temple
ujjain.description: Ancient guardian temple of Ujjain dedicated to Kal Bhairav, the fierce manifestation of Shiva. Famous worldwide for the centuries-old ritual where liquor is offered into the deity mouth.
ujjain.address: Jail Road, Bhairav Garh, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456003, India
ujjain.audio_guide_text: Here stands the fierce protector of Avantika, Kal Bhairav. By custom, all pilgrims seeking blessings in Ujjain pay homage to Bhairav, where daily offerings of consecrated liquid vanish miraculously into the deity stone idol.

ujjain.name: Harsiddhi Mata Temple (Shaktipeeth)
ujjain.description: Sacred 51 Shaktipeeth where Mata Sati elbow fell, historically patronized by legendary King Vikramaditya. Famous for two massive 50-foot Deepstambhas lit with 1,001 lamps during evening aarti.
ujjain.address: Harsiddhi Marg, Jaisinghpura, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456006, India
ujjain.audio_guide_text: Welcome to Harsiddhi Temple, revered as the special kuldevi of Emperor Vikramaditya. Gaze upon the twin multi-tiered stone lamp pillars in the courtyard, which light up every twilight like burning spires of devotion.

ujjain.name: Ram Ghat & Kshipra River Promenade
ujjain.description: Oldest and most sacred bathing ghat on the Shipra River, central site of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela and the mesmerizing evening Kshipra Maha Aarti with floating diyas.
ujjain.address: Ram Ghat, Kshipra River Front, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456006, India
ujjain.audio_guide_text: Ram Ghat on the holy Kshipra River is believed to have welcomed Lord Rama for pitru tarpana during his exile. Every twelve years, millions gather on these stones for the Simhastha Kumbh Snan.

ujjain.name: Maharshi Sandipani Ashram
ujjain.description: Vedic educational hermitage where Lord Krishna, brother Balarama, and friend Sudama mastered 64 arts and 14 sciences in 64 days under Guru Sandipani.
ujjain.address: Mangalnath Road, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456006, India
ujjain.audio_guide_text: Step into Sandipani Ashram, the legendary ancient gurukul where young Krishna inscribed numerals on stone slabs that are still preserved within the premises near the Gomti Kund reservoir.
ujjain.verified_source: Archeological Survey of India & MP Tourism 2026

ujjain.name: Vedh Shala (Jantar Mantar Observatory)
ujjain.description: Built in 1719 by astronomer King Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur, this astronomical observatory marks the ancient Indian Prime Meridian (Tropic of Cancer intersection) with operational stone instruments.
ujjain.best_time_to_visit: 10:00 AM (Clear sunlight for sun dial readings)
ujjain.address: Chintaman Road, Jaisinghpura, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456010, India
ujjain.audio_guide_text: Vedh Shala stands proudly at the historical Greenwich of India. Here, Jai Singh constructed the Samrat Yantra, Digyansha Yantra, and Nadi Valaya to measure planetary motions with astonishing precision.

khatoo.name: Shree Khatu Shyam Ji Mandir (Barbarika Dham)
khatoo.description: Revered pilgrimage shrine dedicated to Barbarika (grandson of Bhima), known as Shyam Baba. Celebrated for miraculous darshan, Phalgun Lakhi Mela, and daily Mangala Aarti.
khatoo.address: Khatu Shyam Ji, Danta Ramgarh Tehsil, Sikar District, Rajasthan 332602, India
khatoo.audio_guide_text: Welcome to Khatu Shyam Ji Mandir, the sacred seat of Sheesh Ke Dani, Lord Barbarika, who sacrificed his head to Lord Krishna before the Mahabharata war. In return, Krishna blessed him with his own name, Shyam, to be worshipped across the Kaliyuga.
khatoo.verified_source: Shri Shyam Mandir Committee Khatoo & Rajasthan Tourism 2026

khatoo.name: Shyam Kund (Sacred Bathing Reservoir)
khatoo.description: The sacred holy pond near the main temple where Barbarika divine head is believed to have surfaced. Devotees take a holy dip here before entering the temple for blessings.
khatoo.address: Near Khatu Shyam Temple, Khatoo, Sikar, Rajasthan 332602, India
khatoo.audio_guide_text: Shyam Kund is the spiritual epicenter of purification in Khatoo. Waters here are considered spiritually purifying, washing away illness and fatigue of visiting pilgrims.

khatoo.name: Gourishankar Temple
khatoo.description: Ancient Lord Shiva shrine adjacent to Shyam Mandir. Legend recalls that Mughal soldiers attempted to spear the Shivalinga, but blood miraculously oozed from the stone, forcing their retreat.
khatoo.address: Temple Complex, Khatoo, Sikar, Rajasthan 332602, India
khatoo.audio_guide_text: Here at Gourishankar Temple, the timeless Shaivite heritage of Khatoo stands preserved. The Shivalinga bears historical battle marks testifying to centuries of steadfast devotion.

khatoo.name: Toran Dwar (Grand Welcome Gate)
khatoo.description: Monumental Rajasthani sandstone ceremonial gateway that marks the entrance to the holy town of Khatoo, where pilgrims unfurl colorful Nishan flags.
khatoo.audio_guide_text: The Toran Dwar welcomes over 5 million pilgrims annually. Passing under this grand archway signifies leaving the material world behind and stepping onto the sacred soil of Shyam Baba.

khatoo.name: Khatoo Dham Prasad & Artisan Bazaar
khatoo.description: Vibrant temple street market brimming with traditional pure desi ghee Churma prasad, sacred Nishan banners, marble idols, and Rajasthani handicrafts.
khatoo.address: Main Market, Khatoo, Sikar, Rajasthan 332602, India
khatoo.audio_guide_text: Immerse yourself in the fragrant aromas of cardamom, saffron, and roasting wheat flour in Khatoo Bazaar, where master sweet-makers prepare Shyam Baba beloved Churma prasad.

khatu.name: Shree Khatu Shyam Ji Mandir (Barbarika Dham)
khatu.description: Revered pilgrimage shrine dedicated to Barbarika (grandson of Bhima), known as Shyam Baba. Celebrated for miraculous darshan, Phalgun Lakhi Mela, and daily Mangala Aarti.
